target: Prevent sandbox process identities from redirecting Windows activation artifacts and require exact post-install shortcut evidence.
primary_semantics: A validated package-provided Skill root is authoritative; fallback identity discovery is permitted only when that root is invalid, and activation is healthy only when the final Shell-resolved shortcut and launcher configuration match live installed paths.
invariants: Raw history, summaries, indexes, cloud state, device trust, and active archive contents remain unchanged.
The existing shortcut name, icon, native launcher, active archive pointer, and user configuration remain preserved.
Shortcut replacement remains atomic and restores the previous shortcut when final verification fails.
v3.0 remains prohibited without its separate incompatible-contract decision.
allowed_changes: Prefer a validated explicit Windows Skill root over process SID discovery.
Inspect Windows Shell shortcut properties after installation.
Add shortcut and launcher configuration checks to the runtime-effect gate.
Extend release rehearsal, documentation, and tests for sandbox-profile activation.
prohibited_changes: Rewrite or delete authoritative memory records.
Accept file existence, process identity, or installer exit code as activation evidence.
Create a shortcut to Python or a console-visible wrapper.
Silently replace a valid explicit Skill root with a service or sandbox profile.
before_after_checks: Resolve the production shortcut and prove all activation paths use the interactive user's installed Skill.
Inject a CodexSandboxOffline shortcut target and prove the runtime-effect gate fails.
Prove an exact live shortcut and launcher configuration pass.
Run full regression, architecture, documentation, same-SHA CI, and installer gates.
